name_reason: Prefix crt_equivalent_ is correct (Watcom CRT wrapper). The descriptor 'exit_chain_stub' is accurate, but the suffix '_36de3' is Ghidra address residue: 0x36de3 is this function's own entry address (read_memory confirms byte 0xC3=RET at 0x36de3; same class as the spec example fd2_noop_stub_4e915). No domain ID is involved (no chapter/item/spell/job/portrait ID, dimension, or multiplier), so the suffix must be dropped. Proposed crt_equivalent_atexit_default_stub keeps the CRT prefix and names the role precisely (the default no-op target the three atexit chain slots point to). Name is free (no collision in src/). Recorded only; rename applied in Stage 2 across protos.h/crtcomp.h + call sites.
purpose: Watcom CRT atexit default no-op handler: a single-byte RET that the three atexit chain slots (0x527d8/0x527dc/0x527e0) point to until atexit(fn) overwrites a slot. When exit/_exit walk the chain via indirect CALL [slot], an unregistered slot lands here and returns immediately, so it is a harmless no-op.
logic_summary: Body is the single instruction RET (0xC3 at 0x36de3). __cdecl, no parameters, no return value, no callee stack cleanup (nothing pushed), no CALL inside (no EAX-tracking concern). Its address is taken as DATA from the three atexit fn-pointer slots (each slot holds little-endian e3 6d 03 00 = 0x00036de3, confirmed via read_memory at 0x527d8), so it must remain a real, callable function and cannot be folded away.

returns.semantics: No return value. Control returns immediately to the indirect CALL site in exit/_exit; the function performs nothing.

comment_original_issue: Original src comment block (lines 348-365) is accurate, precise, and complete: it states the atexit default no-op purpose, the slot-init / chain-walk / atexit-overwrite mechanism, that the address is taken (DATA from the three slots) so it must remain a real callable function, and the __cdecl/no-param/no-return/single-RET/no-EAX-concern details. Matches the Ghidra decompilation and disassembly exactly; no change needed.

This stub itself reads/writes no globals (pure RET).
